$comment: C99/C23 <tgmath.h> (7.25) — FC17.9(g) (D-CSUBSET-TGMATH), complex dispatch added in P46 (D-CSUBSET-TGMATH-COMPLEX, D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX-TO-REAL-IMPLICIT-CONVERSION-REFUSED). Type-generic math over the 17 shipped math.json functions, PURE CONFIG (zero src/ change): each name is a function-like `_Generic` macro (the stdbit.json macro precedent) dispatching float→the f-variant, complex→the <complex.h> function, everything-else→the f64 function. STANDALONE: a TU may include ONLY <tgmath.h>, so this descriptor ships BOTH the macros AND its own symbol rows (duplicate rows vs math.json are first-wins-safe — the size_t ×6 / memcpy ×2 precedent); library map = math.json's (elf libm.so.6 per D-FFI-MATH-LIBM-DT-NEEDED; pe ucrtbase.dll — kept IN LOCKSTEP with math.json, since a TU may include either header and the duplicate rows must not resolve to two different runtime images). ★★★ THE COMPLEX SURFACE, AND WHY IT IS ELEVEN NAMES AND NOT SEVENTEEN. C23 7.25 splits the macros in two, and the split is OBSERVABLE in both references: `sqrt sin cos tan asin acos atan exp log pow fabs` HAVE a <complex.h> counterpart and MUST dispatch to it, while `log10 floor ceil atan2 fmod ldexp` have NONE and must REFUSE. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-31, binaries compiled and RUN, gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x` and clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` probed SEPARATELY: `sqrt(0+4i)` exits 1 (csqrt) on both, `fabs(3+4i)` exits 5 (cabs), `pow(2i,2)` gives -4 (cpow); and all six real-only macros are REJECTED AT COMPILE TIME by both ('no matching function for type-generic call' / 'call to __tg_floor is ambiguous'). So accepting a complex there would put DSS ABOVE the union, and silently dropping the imaginary part into a real prototype is precisely the wrong answer this project ranks below a crash. ★★ HOW THE REFUSAL IS SPELLED, AND WHY IT IS FIRST-CLASS RATHER THAN BORROWED. A real-only macro's `default:` arm is `_Generic((x) + 0.0, double: floor((x)))`. `_Generic`'s controlling expression is UNEVALUATED (C 6.5.1.1p3), so `(x) + 0.0` is a pure TYPE computation: it promotes every real argument — int, char, _Bool, double, and long double on an f64 axis — to `double`, and every complex argument to a COMPLEX type, which matches no association in a list that has no `default:`. That is `S_GenericSelectionNoMatch`, the C 6.5.1.1 constraint itself and the same mechanism gcc and clang refuse with. ⚠ THIS REPLACED A GUARD THAT WORKED FOR THE WRONG REASON: the arm used to be a BARE `floor((x))`, loud only because DSS refused the implicit complex→real conversion one subsystem over — a guard whose loudness came from a DIFFERENT tier's missing feature. That conversion is legal C (6.3.1.7p2), all three references perform it, and P46 admitted it; the loudness had to stop being a side effect and become an owner. ⚠⚠ AND THE OLD RATIONALE FOR THAT BARE ARM WAS REFUTED IN P45, KEPT HERE SO IT IS NOT REINSTATED. It said `(double)z` is 'legal C, silently drops the imaginary part → a conformance MISCOMPILE'. ✔MEASURED: `#include <math.h>` + `sqrt(z)` — the plain `double sqrt(double)` prototype — compiles and exits 0 under gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 AND mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 alike. THE DROP IS CONFORMANT; all three do it. What is not conformant is a <tgmath.h> MACRO reaching a real prototype for a complex argument at all. ⚠⚠ WHY THE `(x) + 0.0` GUARD IS ABSENT FROM THE ELEVEN COMPLEX-CAPABLE MACROS, AND IT IS A MEASURED CONSTRAINT AND NOT AN OVERSIGHT: DSS TYPE-CHECKS A `_Generic`'s UNSELECTED ARMS (this file's own float-arm cast discipline depends on that). On a complex-capable macro the complex arm is the one SELECTED for a complex argument, but `default:` is still CHECKED — so a complex-rejecting guard there refuses every complex call outright (✔MEASURED: eleven S_GenericSelectionNoMatch on the P46 corpus example). A complex can never SELECT `default:` while its own arm exists, so the bare call is correct there. THE ONE COMPLEX THAT STILL REACHES `default:` is a `long double _Complex` on a WALLED long-double axis (element F80/F128, named by neither complex arm) — ✔MEASURED LOUD there anyway, `L_UnsupportedLoweringForOpcode … D-TARGET-ENCODING-WIDTH-GUARD`, on x86_64/x87-80 and arm64/ieee128 alike, the same wall a plain `long double` argument already rides (D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX-MONOMORPH-F64). On an f64 axis `long double _Complex` interns AS `double _Complex` and selects the complex arm, which is why only `double _Complex:` and `float _Complex:` arms exist: adding a `long double _Complex:` arm would DUPLICATE the first one there and break every call (D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-GENERIC-DISTINCT, the same collapse the real arms route around). ★★ THE COMPLEX-BY-VALUE ABI WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE REFERENCES, BECAUSE A MISMATCH HERE IS A SILENT WRONG ANSWER AND NOT A LINK ERROR. ✔MEASURED by disassembling DSS's own output beside each reference's: on elf64-x86_64 DSS passes and returns a `double _Complex` in xmm0/xmm1, exactly as gcc 13.3.0 does (SysV two-SSE-eightbyte); on elf64-aarch64 in d0/d1, exactly as aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc does (AAPCS64 HFA); on pe64 INDIRECTLY — rcx = hidden sret pointer, rdx = pointer to the argument — exactly as mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 does, which is also MSVC's `_Dcomplex` 16-byte-aggregate convention. ★ AND THAT LAST ONE WAS DRIVEN THROUGH THE REAL DLL RATHER THAN INFERRED: ucrtbase.dll's csqrt/cabs/cexp were called through that convention and RUN, returning 1.414214+1.414214i, 5.000000 and 1.000000+0.000000i. ★ THE ELEVEN COMPLEX ROWS ARE ORDINARY EXTERN LIBCALLS — the setjmp/threads FFI precedent, no new lowering and no builtin. ✔MEASURED PRESENT: all eleven are in ucrtbase.dll's export table (objdump -p), and all eleven are dynamic symbols of libm.so.6 as WEAK `W` with a GLIBC version suffix (weak is safe under the eager-import law; ABSENT is not). ★★ THE MACHO ARMS WERE GATED OFF THE COMPLEX PATH UNTIL 2026-08-31, AND THE REASON THEY CAME BACK ON IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A DECISION. P46's first landing shipped the eleven rows `availableObjectFormats: [pe, elf]`, with each macho arm taking the real-only shape, so a complex argument there was `S_GenericSelectionNoMatch`: LOUD, never a wrong answer, and BELOW clang on that one platform rather than silently divergent from it. That was a MEASUREMENT gap, not a platform one, and this repo owns the instrument that named it: `tests/ffi/test_darwin_link_name_oracle` requires every Mach-O-visible imported function to have a row in `tests/ffi/data/darwin-link-names.tsv` recording what a REAL Darwin compiler emits for that identifier, per arch — and it REFUSED all eleven when they were first shipped ungated. ★ THE ORACLE WAS RIGHT AND WAS NOT ROUTED AROUND: an export check cannot settle this class, because a WRONG-but-EXISTING spelling links clean, loads clean and misbinds SILENTLY — the `_fstat` vs `_fstat$INODE64` case that made sqlite call every database malformed. ✔THE MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN (cycle P46, lane `dw`) on macOS 26.6.2, Apple clang 21.0.0, both arches, by the recipe the oracle prints in its own failure message: all eleven emit the PLAIN decorated identifier (`_csqrt`, `_cabs`, …) on x86_64 AND on arm64, so every one implies an ABSENT `linkName`. ★ THAT ANSWER IS WHY THE GATE WAS RIGHT RATHER THAN PARANOID: "they are probably plain" would have been CORRECT and still worthless — the same reasoning applied to `stat` is what bound the legacy 32-bit-inode callee. An absent measurement and a measurement that came back plain are different states, and only one of them is evidence. ✔ALSO MEASURED in the same session, because DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every function a descriptor lists and one ABSENT symbol breaks the LOAD of every binary including this header: all eleven LINK against libSystem on both arches, and csqrt/cabs/cpow were RUN natively returning 1.414214+1.414214i, 5.000000 and -4.000000+0.000000i — the values libm.so.6 and ucrtbase.dll already produce for the same inputs. ⇒ the gate is GONE from the eleven rows and each macho arm now carries the text its elf arm already carried, which is why elf and macho are byte-identical for these eleven and only `fabs`/`ldexp` still differ per format (pe alone lacks fabsf/ldexpf). D-CSUBSET-TGMATH-COMPLEX closes on exactly this. ★ THE CAST DISCIPLINE ON THE FLOAT ARM IS UNCHANGED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: `_Generic`'s UNSELECTED arms are fully type-checked, so a naked `sqrtf((x))` arm would reject a legal f64 call via the arm's F64→F32 narrowing (S_TypeMismatch); the explicit `(float)` cast is what keeps it legal. No `double:`/`long double:` arms exist AT ALL, so the f64-format long-double≡double intern collapse (D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-GENERIC-DISTINCT) is structurally routed around — the stdbit width-routing precedent; integer args ride the `(x) + 0.0` promotion or the bare `default:` (C 7.25p3: any non-float real arg → the double version). The self-reference (`default: sqrt((x))` inside `#define sqrt(x)`) is Prosser-blue-painted (no re-expansion) and binds this descriptor's own extern row. TWO-ARG (pow/atan2/fmod): nested `_Generic` — BOTH args float → the f-variant with `(float)` casts on both; ANY other combo → the bare f64 fn. `pow` carries the complex arms in BOTH positions, because C23 7.25p3 says EITHER argument being complex invokes `cpow`. `ldexp` dispatches on arg 1 only: arg 2 is an `int` and NOT a generic parameter, so it is deliberately UNGUARDED — ✔MEASURED, gcc and clang both ACCEPT `ldexp(3.0, z)` and convert the complex exponent to int (exit 12), and DSS now exits 12 there too. ★ PE GAP (D-CSUBSET-MATH-FLOAT-VARIANTS-PE) — UNCHANGED BY THE UCRT MIGRATION: NEITHER pe C runtime exports fabsf/ldexpf (objdump -p verified absent from msvcrt.dll AND from ucrtbase.dll), so the pe `variants` arms route the float arm THROUGH the f64 function with an EXACT round-trip: |x| and 2^n·x of any F32 are exactly representable in F64, so `(float)fabs((double)(x))` / `(float)ldexp((double)(x),(y))` return bit-identical results to fabsf/ldexpf. The other 15 f-variants ARE pe exports (runtime-witnessed) → ungated rows. SURFACE (D-CSUBSET-TGMATH-SURFACE): the C23 7.25 names NOT in math.json (frexp/modf/round/trunc/hypot/cbrt/exp2/log2/lround/remainder/the cosh-sinh-tanh family and their complex twins, and the C23 _Decimal names) are NOT shipped and fail LOUD by absence (S_UndeclaredIdentifier on use); <tgmath.h> nominally includes <math.h>+<complex.h> (7.25p1) — a consumer needing INFINITY/I includes those headers directly (same -SURFACE row). ⚠ <complex.h> ITSELF STILL SHIPS NO LIBCALL SURFACE: `#include <complex.h>` + `csqrt(z)` remains S_UndeclaredIdentifier, which is D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX-TRANSCENDENTAL and is NOT closed by this file — the eleven rows here are tgmath's own, exactly as the 34 real rows are.
